To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the rGO electrodeposited on the glassy carbon electrode (GCE) surface was used to immobilize UCNPs and MIPs, which were synthesized using CLB as template and methacrylic acid (MAA) as functional monomer.

a novel ECL sensor based on molecularly imprinted polymer (MIP) was developed for the determination of clenbutrol (CLB) by using rGO-UCNPs as the ECL emitter and the MIP was prepared by the copolymerization of methacrylamide (MAA) and 4-vinylpyridine (4-VP) in the presence of CLB template.

the proposed MIECLS based on electrodeposited rGObased UCNPs-ECLS and MIP exhibited excellent sensitivity, desirable selectivit and favorable stability, which indicated enormous potential in the food safety detection.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an ultrasensitive MIECLS based on rGO-UCNPs for the detection of CLB.
a novel ECL sensing platform for CLB determination.
the development of a new type of MIP based on the ECL signal of UCNPs and rGO, which provides a new idea and method for the development of new MIECL sensors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the developed sensor has the potential to be applied for CLB detection in real samples.
the proposed MIECLS is an excellent tool for the determination of CLB in food samples.
the MIECLS was developed based on rGO and UCNPs, and it could provide a promising strategy for the detection of CLB.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MIECLS was successfully fabricated by electrodeposition of rGO, UCNPs-ECLS and MIP.

a simple and effective strategy for the fabrication of a molecularly imprinted sensor based on UCNPs-ECLS was developed for the first time, which provided a novel and promising way for ultrasensitive detection and analysis of trace analytes.
a novel and simple ECL sensor was successfully fabricated by using rGO electrodeposited graphene oxide, upconversion nanoparticles, and molecularly imprinted technique.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have successfully constructed a MIECLS by using UCNPs and rGO as the ECL emitter and the electrodeposited carrier.
UCNPs-ECLS combined with MIP could be a new strategy for developing highly sensitive and specific sensors.
the proposed MIECLS based on rGO-UCNPs and MIP has a great potential to be used for the detection of CLB in real samples.
